[March 4th, 2026 9:44 AM] hrusi: <@U09104V5VR9> <@U08HPM99N80> the reason I wanted to avoid any sort of indicator is that we won't know when the user has watched something fully. We would first need to have have watch duration tracking, then come up with some rules on how much percentage counts as "watched" - e.g., 10%, 50%, 75%

A scroll state/resume state avoids the complexity of tracking watch percentage, then figuring out what constitutes a "fully watched state".

And if we agree on resuming the scroll, it also takes out the complexity of shuffling cards - user simply is taken to the last video they were on and from there they can do whatever they want to do.

Also avoids the surprises of where did my video go?

Thank you guys!
Also, are you guys familiar with Semantic Coloring?
We are toying with the idea of creating a "Design Provider" on our code, a centralized place were we'd be able to fetch icons / images, colors and fonts for the entire app.
This way if we are to change styling in the future, we can just change it in this centralized provider and the whole app will "magically" conform to the new styling.

But for that to work well with the colors, instead of using the color tokens themselves (`.heat500`, `.buzz800` etc) when rendering the components, we'd be better off using semantic colors such as `text-primary`, `critical`, `background-inactive` and so on.
Is this something that we can think about in the future? :slightly_smiling_face:

mentioned there has been some brand and strategy sessions lately that'll influence our palette in the future so fingers crossed for that feedback.
